title: XPENG Launches "YOYO" Robotaxi
source_used: CarNewsChina (8 Oct 2026) and Future Transport-News (9 Oct 2026); CleanTechnica was blocked
key_facts: Xpeng named its robotaxi service Yoyo on 8 Oct 2026 and opened it to users in China through an invitation-based program, according to chief executive He Xiaopeng.
The GX-based vehicle has completed more than 2,200 trial rides by employees; the announcement gave no fleet size and no date for unrestricted public service.
Riders book pilot slots through a ride-hailing mini-program (a small app inside a larger app) using invitation codes.

The robotaxi uses four in-house Turing AI chips and the second-generation VLA 2.0 model, with a vision-based system and no lidar or high-definition maps; Xpeng describes it as designed for Level 4 driving.
In August Xpeng obtained a Guangzhou qualification to test without a safety operator in the driver's seat on designated test roads.
Xpeng plans to earn revenue from vehicle sales, technology services and a share of operating revenue, while partners run local fleets.
Xpeng is discussing partnerships in Europe, the Middle East and Southeast Asia; no overseas partners or launch dates were named.
He has said the Guangzhou robotaxi business could break even at vehicle level in the second half of 2027.
quote_evidence: Xpeng named its robotaxi service Yoyo (小鹏悠游) on October 8 and opened it to users in China through an invitation-based program, according to company CEO He Xiaopeng.
The announcement did not disclose the fleet size or a date for unrestricted public service.
The company previously set a 2027 target for passenger services without safety drivers.
why_it_matters_hint: A first step toward paid driverless taxi service in China, with fleet size, public opening date and safety record still unknown.
notes: Pooled item is CleanTechnica's 10 Oct piece (HTTP 403, not read). Same story read at CarNewsChina and Future Transport-News. Already carried in our 8 Oct (CnEVPost) and 9 Oct (TechNode) editions.
